concept.title: Navigation and the home page
concept.shortdesc: Every page carries a sidebar tree built from your map; the home page is generated from the map's own metadata.

section.title: The sidebar
section.p: navigationsidebarmobile menuThe sidebar lists the whole publication, follows your map's hierarchy, and marks the page being read. With JavaScript available it gains a menu toggle on small screens and expand/collapse controls on branches, with the current page's ancestors open; without JavaScript the full tree simply stays visible, so nothing is ever unreachable.

Topics with toc="no" stay out of the tree but are still built and linkable — useful for large reference sets addressed by cross-reference rather than browsing, as in the Open Referral UK publications.
An entry that appears as plain text with nothing beneath it usually means a key the toolkit never resolved; the build warns (GOVK001W) and explains the cause and the fix.

section.title: The home page
section.p: The site's index.html chooses its layout from the map's shape: a single top-level entry gets a hero page with a green start button, a few entries get an annotated contents list, and many entries — or a bookmap with several chapters, like this manual — get grouped sections. The govuk.homepage.layout parameter overrides the choice, including a column grid and an accordion for very large publications. Bookmaps contribute more: the alternative book title becomes the abstract paragraph, and the book's author and owning organisation appear beneath it — exactly as on this manual's own home page. shows every layout as a screenshot of this manual.
section.note: Give each top-level topic a good shortdesc: the richer layouts reuse it as the entry's description, as this manual's home page shows.
